_comment: Production advisories the npm audit gate may pass over, and only while the
reason below stays true. Same discipline as osv-scanner.toml (CLAUDE.md rule
54): every entry carries an expiry and a reason that was verified, not
assumed. An expired entry FAILS the gate -- that is the point, because a
suppression nobody revisits is a decision made once and inherited forever.
An entry belongs here only when the vulnerable code path is unreachable in
this application and that is checkable. 'We think it is fine' is not a

allow.reason: resolveContent() on a MailMessage bypasses disableFileAccess when resolving ATTACHMENT content. Holt never sends attachments: src/lib/email/sender.ts calls sendMail({ from, to, subject, html }) and passes no attachments key on any path. Pinned by __tests__/emailNoAttachments.test.ts, which fails if an attachments option is ever introduced -- at which point this suppression stops being true and must go. Upstream fix is nodemailer 10.x, a major bump that gets its own session (rule 5).
